// Cocktail Shaker Sort

a1 = arr[5, 1, 4, 2, 8]

fun Cocktail_Shaker_Sort(@init<table> array):
    n = length(array)
    swapped = True
    start = 0
    end = n - 1

    while (swapped):
        swapped = False

        for (i = start; i < end; i += 1):
            @mark<i, outline, yellow> if (array[i] > array[i + 1]):
                @mark<i, highlight, green> swap(array[i], array[i + 1])
                swapped = True
            end if
        end for

        if (not swapped):
            break
        end if

        swapped = False
        end = end - 1

        for (i = end - 1; i >= start; i -= 1):
            @mark<i, outline, yellow> if (array[i] > array[i + 1]):
                @mark<i, highlight, green> swap(array[i], array[i + 1])
                swapped = True
            end if
        end for

        start = start + 1
    end while

    return array
end fun

result = Cocktail_Shaker_Sort(a1)
```

This implementation of Cocktail Shaker Sort alternates between sorting passes from left to right and right to left, ensuring that the largest unsorted element bubbles up to its correct position in each pass. The visualization directives help track the swapping and marking of elements during the sorting process.

fun Cocktail_Shaker_Sort(@init<table> array):
    n = length(array)
    swapped = True
    start = 0
    end = n - 1

    while (swapped):

                @mark<i, highlight, green> swap(array[i], array[i + 1])
                swapped = True
            end if
        end for

        if (not swapped):
            break
        end if

        swapped = False
        end = end - 1

        for (i = end - 1; i >= start; i -= 1):
            @mark<i, outline, yellow> if (array[i] > array[i + 1]):
                @mark<i, highlight, green> swap(array[i], array[i + 1])
                swapped = True
            end if
        end for

        start = start + 1
    end while

    return array

        for (i = 0, i < n - 1, i += 1):

// Dutch National Flag Problem

a1 = arr[0, 2, 1, 2, 0]

fun Dutch_National_Flag(@init<table> array):
    n = length(array)
    
    low = 0
    mid = 0
    high = n - 1
    
    while (mid <= high):
        @mark<mid, outline, yellow> switch (array[mid]):
            case 0:
                @mark<low, highlight, green> swap(array[low], array[mid])
                low += 1
                mid += 1
                break
            case 1:
                mid += 1
                break
            case 2:
                @mark<high, highlight, green> swap(array[mid], array[high])
                high -= 1
                break
        end switch
    end while
    return array
end fun

result = Dutch_National_Flag(a1)
```

This code sorts an array of 0s, 1s, and 2s in a single pass using the Dutch National Flag algorithm. The `Dutch_National_Flag` function uses three pointers (`low`, `mid`, and `high`) to partition the array into three parts: elements less than 1, elements equal to 1, and elements greater than 1. The `swap` function is used to exchange elements as needed. The final sorted array is returned.

fun Merge(@init<table> array, l, m, r):
    n1 = m - l + 1
    n2 = r - m

    L = arr[n1]
    R = arr[n2]

    i = 0
    j = 0
    k = l

    while (i < n1 and j < n2):
        @mark<i, outline, yellow> if (L[i] <= R[j]):
            @mark<k, highlight, green> array[k] = L[i]
            i += 1
        else:
            @mark<k, highlight, green> array[k] = R[j]
            j += 1
        end if
        k += 1
    end while

    while (i < n1):
        @mark<k, highlight, green> array[k] = L[i]
        i += 1
        k += 1
    end while

    while (j < n2):
        @mark<k, highlight, green> array[k] = R[j]
        j += 1
        k += 1
    end while
end fun

fun Merge_Sort(@init<table> array, l, r):
    if (l < r):
        m = floor((l + r) / 2)

        Merge_Sort(array, l, m)
        Merge_Sort(array, m + 1, r)

        Merge(array, l, m, r)
    end if
end fun

end fun

        end if

    end if

end fun
